To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sexual risk behaviors and the contexts in which these behaviors occur among young HIV-infected MSM are complex.

the social sexual environment, substance use, psychological factors, and characteristics of sexual partners were associated with high risk sexual behavior among HIV-infected young Black and Latino MSM.

(1) substance use, social-sexual-environments, and partner characteristics are associated with risky sexual behavior among young men who have HIV; (2) the majority of participants reported that they had reduced risky sexual behavior after they learned of their HIV status; and (3) the subset of participants who continued to have risky sexual behavior reported multiple factors that were associated with these behaviors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the sexual risk behaviors and HIV prevention needs of youths living with AIDS, particularly those who continue to practice high-risk sexual behaviors.
the role of substance abuse in the sexual behaviors of young people living with HIV, and the impact of the social environment on sexual risk behaviors among young people living with the virus.
the sexual risk behaviors and the associated factors among HIV-infected youth, and the implications for secondary prevention of HIV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

substance use, the sexual environment, and partner characteristics play an important role in the sexual risk behaviors among youths living with HIV and that these factors should be considered in designing interventions for HIV-infected youth.
the study of the role of social environmental factors in sexual risk behaviors among HIV-infected youths is an important and underdeveloped area of research that should be pursued.
the social environment, substance abuse, mental health issues, and partner characteristics all play a significant role in the sexual behaviors of young men living with HIV/AIDS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there was no one single factor that explained the high-risk sexual behavior of these young men.

the social environment, the psychological impact, substance use, and partner characteristics are associated with sexual risk behaviors in this group, and that these factors cluster in the high-risk group.

the majority of the young men who have been living with HIV for a long time are now in a place where they are able to reduce their risky sexual behavior, but there is a subgroup that is continuing to have unprotected sex with multiple partners.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are multiple levels that need to be addressed in HIV prevention interventions for young men who have HIV, including substance use, social environmental factors, mental health, and partner factors.
the social context in which risky sexual behaviors occur is important to understand.

the majority of young men who have had unprotected sex since their HIV diagnosis had multiple reasons for this behavior and that the reasons were complex, interwoven, and often related to their social and sexual environment.
